consensus_summary: Primary consensus meaning is a committed learner/follower of Jesus (self-denial, cross-bearing, abiding in his word, love, fruit-bearing), often synonymous with Christian (Acts 11:26); common alternatives are the Twelve specifically, any ancient adherent of a teacher, or literary stand-ins for the church.
book_summary: One in whom the law is sealed (Isa 8:16), proven by continuing in the word, love, and fruit; one who meets the thrice-stated conditions of leaving own, bearing the cross, and forsaking all; baptized into the Name and perfected as his master—the One in whom the Name, covenant, and law dwell.
book_core_identification: One in whom the law is sealed (Name/covenant dwelling therein), perfected as the Master
boundary_disagreement: Book makes OT sealing of the law and indwelling of the Name/covenant definitional to the identity of a disciple; consensus sets boundaries solely by NT relational following, cost, and Acts usage without treating the sealing motif as core.
material_contradiction: None; the book affirms the same NT marks and the common-view note of learner/follower.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the same general referent (true disciples marked by John 8:31 continuance, love/fruit, and Luke 14 cost conditions) while the book materially refines precision and framing by elevating Isa 8:16 sealing plus Name/covenant indwelling as the essential identification and linking perfection to the Master of Ex 23:21. This changes boundary conditions and symbolic density without replacing the referent or creating contradiction, so REFINED rather than MATCH, DIVERGENT, or NOVEL. Extension covers the same cases of true disciples.
strongest_objection: Isa 8:16 and related OT sealing/Name texts are not employed by the NT to define ‘disciple,’ making the book’s core an allegorical imposition rather than the term’s ordinary biblical sense; consensus rightly treats the word as a straightforward relational designation.
